lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, Healthy body, happy mind! Today, we follow the rainbow from the Village of Springs. We climb up, up, up, above the clouds. Look! The rainbow is a huge bridge! But its colors are very pale. An old white crane flies down to meet us. Her name is Iris. She is the keeper of the bridge. She says, Welcome to the Rainbow Bridge! This bridge connects many countries. Say it with me. This bridge connects many countries. Wonderful! Kiko asks, Why are the colors so pale? Iris answers, Not many friends visit now. Let's read the sign at the bridge gate. "Welcome to the Rainbow Bridge! This bridge connects many countries. Please walk to Friendship Plaza in the middle. Meet new friends and share your stories. Every kind word brings back one color. When all seven colors shine, the bridge will be happy again. From Iris, Keeper of the Bridge." Where is Friendship Plaza? In the middle of the bridge. How many colors are there? Seven. Now, phonics. Today, we listen to words we use in Japanese, too. But English sounds different! Energy. EN-er-gy. Not e-ne-ru-gi. Allergy. AL-ler-gy. Vitamin. VI-ta-min. Hamburger. HAM-bur-ger. Say the strong part loudly. Let's walk to Friendship Plaza!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, This bridge connects many countries. Today, we arrive at Friendship Plaza in the middle of the bridge. Three children are waiting for us. Aino is from Finland. She says, Moi! Amara is from Kenya. She says, Jambo! Mateo is from Mexico. He says, Hola! Birimo is our interpreter. Moi, Jambo, Hola! That means hello, hello, hello! Before we sit down on the soft carpet, Haru takes off his shoes. He says, In Japan, we take off our shoes at home. Say it with me. In Japan, we take off our shoes at home. Great! Aino smiles. In my family, we take off our shoes, too. It's the same! Mateo says, In my family, we wear slippers at home. Iris says, Every family is different. Let's read the plaza board. "Friendship Plaza Rules. Please say hello in your own language. Ask questions about your new friends. Listen carefully and smile. Some things are the same. Some things are different. Both are wonderful! Please take off your shoes on the blue carpet. Thank you! From Iris." Where do you take off your shoes? On the blue carpet. What should you do with new friends? Ask questions and listen. Now, phonics. Camera. CAM-er-a. Not ka-me-ra. Video. VID-e-o. Radio. RA-di-o. Calendar. CAL-en-dar. Say the strong part loudly. Same or different? Let's find out!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, In Japan, we take off our shoes at home. Today, we talk about school life on the bridge. Riko says, In Japan, the school year starts in April. How about in your country? Say it with me. How about in your country? Wonderful! Amara says, At my school, the school year starts in January. Mateo says, In Mexico, it starts in late August. Aino says, In Finland, children start school at seven. Kiko is surprised. Seven? Wow! Then Haru says, In Japan, we clean our classroom. Mateo says, That's cool! Let's read Amara's school card. "Jambo! I'm Amara. At my school, the school year starts in January. We wear green uniforms. Our first class starts at eight. My favorite subject is science, because I love the stars. After school, I go running with my friends. How about in your country? Please tell me!" When does Amara's school year start? In January. What is her favorite subject? Science. Now, phonics. These words sound different in English, too. Idea. i-DE-a. Not a-i-de-a. Piano. pi-AN-o. Museum. mu-SE-um. Volunteer. vol-un-TEER. The strong part is in the middle or at the end. Let's ask our new friends more questions!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, How about in your country? Today, it's lunchtime on the bridge. Everyone opens a lunch box. Haru uses chopsticks. Mateo eats a tortilla with his hands. He says, In Mexico, I eat tortillas with my hands. Kiko says, That's interesting! We do it differently（ちがう やりかたで）. We use chopsticks. Say it with me. That's interesting! We do it differently. Great! Mateo asks, Can you show me? Haru shows him how to hold chopsticks. Then Mateo shows Haru how to fold a tortilla. Riko says, Let's try it your way! Aino says, At my school, lunch is free for everyone. Let's read today's lunch menu. "Friendship Plaza Lunch. Today we have rice balls from Japan, tortillas with beans from Mexico, fish soup from Finland, and chapati from Kenya. You can use chopsticks, a fork, a spoon, or your hands. Try something new today! For dessert, there is vanilla ice cream." What is from Finland? Fish soup. What is for dessert? Vanilla ice cream. Now, phonics. Vanilla. va-NIL-la. Pajamas. pa-JA-mas. Spaghetti. spa-GHET-ti. Macaroni. mac-a-RO-ni. Say the strong part loudly and a little longer. Let's try new food together!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, That's interesting! We do it differently. Today, we make a culture comparison chart. Riko draws a big chart on the plaza board. Japan and Finland. What's the same? What's different? Aino says, In Finland, people watch fireworks on New Year's Eve. Haru says, In Japan, we eat soba on New Year's Eve. Then Kiko says, In both countries, people celebrate New Year. Say it with me. In both countries, people celebrate New Year. Fantastic! Let's read the chart. "Culture Comparison Chart: Japan and Finland. New Year's Eve: In Japan, many people eat soba. In Finland, many people watch fireworks. School starts: April in Japan, August in Finland. Shoes at home: In both countries, people take off their shoes. Winter: Both countries have lots of snow!" When does school start in Finland? In August. What is the same? Shoes at home and snow. Everyone claps. Look! A red light runs across the bridge. The first color is back! Iris says, Thank you, friends. Every friend is a color. Now, phonics review. Energy. EN-er-gy. Camera. CAM-er-a. Idea. i-DE-a. Spaghetti. spa-GHET-ti. One color is back. Six more to go!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, In both countries, people celebrate New Year. Today, Kiko opens her lunch box. Mateo points and asks, What's that? Kiko says, Onigiri is a kind of rice ball. Say it with me. Onigiri is a kind of rice ball. Wonderful! Kiko says, You can put salmon or umeboshi inside. Aino asks, What's it like? Haru says, It's salty and delicious. Then Birimo eats one, two, three, four onigiri! Birimo, slow down! Let's read Kiko's food cards. "Japanese Food Cards. Onigiri is a kind of rice ball. You can put salmon, tuna, or umeboshi inside. Umeboshi is a sour pickled plum. Miso soup is a kind of soup. It has tofu and green onions in it. Mochi is a kind of rice cake. It is soft and sticky. Enjoy!" What is umeboshi? A sour pickled plum. What is in the miso soup? Tofu and green onions. Now, phonics. English speakers use some Japanese words, too! Sushi. We write s h i for shi. Tofu. We write f u for fu. Tempura. Before p, we write m, not n. Bento. It's a boxed lunch. Let's explain more Japanese food to our friends!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, Onigiri is a kind of rice ball. Today, Kiko takes out a beautiful square cloth. Amara asks, What is it used for? Kiko says, A furoshiki is used for wrapping things. Say it with me. A furoshiki is used for wrapping things. Great! It's made of cloth. You can carry a lunch box in it. Kiko ties the corners, and it becomes a bag! Haru shows a paper fan. It's used for cooling your face. Riko shows chopsticks. They're used for eating. Let's read the labels at the Japan table. "Japanese Tools. Furoshiki: It's used for wrapping and carrying things. It's made of cloth. You can use it again and again. Uchiwa: It's a paper fan. It's used for cooling your face on hot days. Chopsticks: They're used for eating. Please touch them and try!" What is a furoshiki made of? Cloth. What is an uchiwa used for? Cooling your face. Now, phonics. These Japanese words are English words, too! Origami. In English, we say o-ri-GA-mi. Futon. We write f u for fu. Kimono. ki-MO-no. Emoji. We write j i for ji. Let's wrap something together!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, Welcome to Japan! Let me show you around. Our video was a big hit on the bridge! Today, we talk about our favorite seasons at Friendship Plaza. Iris asks, Which season is the best? Haru says, I think summer is the best season because we can swim in the sea. Say it with me. I think summer is the best season because we can swim in the sea. Wonderful! First, say what you think. Then, say because and give a reason. Aino says, I think winter is the best because I love snow. In Finland, winter is long and white. Amara asks, Why do you think so? Aino laughs and says, Because skiing is so much fun! Let's read the seasons board on the plaza. "Our Favorite Seasons. Haru likes summer because he can swim in the sea. Aino likes winter because she loves snow and skiing. Amara likes the rainy season because the plants grow fast. Mateo likes fall because his birthday is in October. Every season is someone's favorite!" Why does Amara like the rainy season? Because the plants grow fast. When is Mateo's birthday? In October. Now, phonics. Listen to the rhythm. I like SUMMER and WINTER. And is small and quick. I want to SWIM in the SEA. To is weak. It's the BEST SEASON for SWIMMING. For is short. We can SEE FIREWORKS in SUMMER. Can is soft. Big words are strong. Small words are weak. Which season do you like best?

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, I think summer is the best season because we can swim in the sea. Today, it's lunchtime on the bridge. Kiko shows a photo of a Japanese school lunch. Rice, miso soup, fish, and milk. Mateo says, Wow! You eat lunch in your classroom? Haru says, Yes. We serve lunch to our classmates. Then Riko gives her opinion（いけん）. In my opinion, school lunch is great. Say it with me. In my opinion, school lunch is great. Excellent! In my opinion means I think. It's a polite way to start. Aino says, In my opinion, we should have more time to eat. At my school in Finland, lunch is free for every student. Let's read Kiko's lunch menu card. "Friday School Lunch. Rice and a small bowl of miso soup. Grilled fish with lemon. Salad with corn and carrots. A carton of milk. Dessert is an orange. Lunch starts at twelve fifteen. Students serve the food and clean up together. Please eat everything and say thank you!" What is the dessert? An orange. What time does lunch start? At twelve fifteen. Now, phonics. Listen to the rhythm. We have a BOWL of RICE. Of is tiny. We eat LUNCH at SCHOOL. At is quick. Do you want RICE or BREAD? Or is soft. We serve LUNCH to our CLASSMATES. To is weak. What's your opinion about school lunch?

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, In my opinion, school lunch is great. Today, Iris has a question for everyone on the plaza. Which is better, a summer vacation at the sea or a winter vacation in the snow? Haru says, The sea is better. Then he asks, Do you agree? Say it with me. Do you agree? Great! Riko says, Yes, I agree. Kiko says, Me too! But Aino says, I'm not sure. I see your point, but I like winter better. Everyone smiles. It's OK to have different opinions. We listen, and we speak kindly. Let's read Iris's sign about talking rules. "Friendship Plaza Talking Rules. Listen to the end. Don't stop your friend in the middle. Say I agree, or say I'm not sure. Use kind words, like I see your point. Give a reason for your opinion. Different ideas make our bridge brighter. Thank you!" What should you do first? Listen to the end. What makes the bridge brighter? Different ideas. Now, phonics. Listen to the rhythm. What do you THINK of my IDEA? Of is tiny. Can I ASK a QUESTION? Can is soft. I was SURPRISED at FIRST. Was is quick. Are your REASONS the SAME? Are is weak. Different opinions, kind words!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, Do you agree? Today, we learn a strong way to give an opinion. Give two reasons! Amara loves running. She walks to school every day. Haru says, I think walking to school is good. First, it's fun. Second, it's good for our health. Say it with me. First, it's fun. Second, it's good for our health. Super! First and second make your opinion clear. Mateo asks, Do you have another reason? Riko says, Yes. We can talk with friends. Let's read Amara's opinion card. "Walking to School, by Amara. I think walking to school is great. First, it's good for my health. My legs are strong, so I can run fast in races. Second, I can see beautiful things on the way. I see birds, trees, and the morning sky. I walk with my sister every day. It's my favorite time." What is her first reason? It's good for her health. Who does she walk with? Her sister. Now, phonics. Listen to the rhythm. It's GOOD for our HEALTH. For is short. It's FUN to COOK with FRIENDS. To is weak. VEGETABLES are GOOD for your BODY. Are is quick. Let's ASK them to HELP. Them is soft. First, practice. Second, have fun!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, First, it's fun. Second, it's good for our health. Today is Opinion Corner on the Rainbow Bridge! There is a little stage in the middle of Friendship Plaza. Each friend gives an opinion with two reasons. Kiko goes first. I think picnics are the best. First, the food is tasty. Second, we can play outside. Say it with me. I think picnics are the best. First, the food is tasty. Second, we can play outside. Fantastic! Then Kiko says, Thank you for listening. Do you agree? Mateo says, That's a good point! Kiko says, Thank you. Look! The bridge is shining. The yellow color is back! Let's read the Opinion Corner program. "Opinion Corner on the Bridge. Speaker one, Kiko: Picnics are the best. Speaker two, Mateo: Drawing is a great hobby. Speaker three, Aino: Everyone should try a sauna. Speaker four, Birimo: Snacks are important. Each speaker has one minute. Please listen quietly and clap at the end." How long does each speaker have? One minute. What is Mateo's topic? Drawing. Now, phonics. We can SEE FIREWORKS in SUMMER. Can is soft. What do you THINK of my IDEA? Of is tiny. Ninja. English speakers use this Japanese word too. Vitamin. VI-ta-min. Say the VI part strongly. Great speeches, everyone!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, I think picnics are the best. First, the food is tasty. Second, we can play outside. Today is a special day for Haru. Do you remember Leo? He is Haru's pen pal from the Tower of Messages. They wrote emails, but they have never talked face to face. Today, Iris turns on the big screen at Friendship Plaza. It's a video call! Leo waves from his home near the snowy mountains. Haru says, It's nice to finally see you! Say it with me. It's nice to finally see you! Wonderful! Then Haru asks, Can you hear me? Leo says, Yes, loud and clear! Sometimes the sound is bad. Then we say, Sorry, could you say that again? Let's read Iris's card about video call manners. "Video Call Manners. Find a quiet place. Look at the camera and smile. Wave hello at the start. If the sound is bad, ask, Could you say that again? Wait for your turn to speak. Use the mute button when it's noisy. Don't share your address or your school name. Say goodbye with a wave." Where should you look? At the camera. What should you not share? Your address or your school name. Now, phonics. Meet you. Meet-chu! The t and the y join. Could you. Could-joo. Would you. Would-joo. Did you. Did-joo. Nice to meet you, everyone!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, It's nice to finally see you! Today, Kiko has a surprise. Last night, she folded paper cranes for our new friends. She gives one to Amara. I've made this for you. It's a paper crane. Say it with me. I've made this for you. It's a paper crane. Beautiful! Amara asks, What is it made of? Kiko says, It's made of paper. In Japan, cranes mean long life. Amara says, Thank you! I'll keep it forever. Then Iris laughs. Iris is a crane, too! She says, Now I have many little sisters! Let's read the card with the cranes. "To Aino, Amara, and Mateo. These are paper cranes. They are a kind of origami. We made them from one square of paper. No scissors and no glue! In Japan, people sometimes fold one thousand cranes for a wish. Our wish is easy. Please keep in touch! From Kiko and friends." How many cranes do people fold for a wish? One thousand. What is their wish? Keep in touch. Now, phonics. A kind of. A-kind-of. The words hold hands. Made of. Made-of. Put it on. Pu-ti-ton. Keep in touch. Kee-pin-touch. Let's fold a crane together!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, I've made this for you. It's a paper crane. Today, there is a mystery on the bridge! Aino says, My scarf is gone! Where did it go? Do you remember the Cave of Riddles? We are good detectives now. First, Riko finds a clue. It's a blue thread on the railing. Then, everyone is quiet. Suddenly, they hear a noise. Peep, peep! Haru says, First, we found a clue. Suddenly, we heard a noise. It must be a bird! Say it with me. First, we found a clue. Suddenly, we heard a noise. It must be a bird! Excellent! Kiko looks up and says, Look! A baby bird is sleeping in it. The scarf is a warm nest! Let's read Riko's detective notes. "The Case of the Missing Scarf. Clue one: a blue thread on the railing. Clue two: small feathers near the lamp. Clue three: a peep peep sound from above. Answer: a mother bird took the scarf. Now her baby is warm and happy. Aino says the bird can keep it. Case closed!" What was clue two? Small feathers near the lamp. Who took the scarf? A mother bird. Now, phonics. Bus stop. Say the s sound only once. Take care. One k sound. Good day. One d sound. Hot tea. One t sound. Great detective work, everyone!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, First, we found a clue. Suddenly, we heard a noise. It must be a bird! Today, we talk about experiences. Do you remember the Cloudtop Railway? We asked, Have you ever seen a rainbow train? Now, Haru asks Mateo, Have you ever made sushi? Say it with me. Have you ever made sushi? Great! Mateo says, No, I haven't. But I've made tacos many times! Then Mateo says, I've played soccer since I was six. In the Village of Springs, we learned since. Do you remember? Amara says, I've never seen snow. Aino smiles and says, You should come to Finland! Let's read the bingo card on the plaza. "Experience Bingo. Find a friend for each box. Have you ever seen snow? Have you ever ridden a train above the clouds? Have you ever made a paper crane? Have you ever been on a stage? Have you ever eaten tacos? Write your friend's name in the box. Get five in a row and shout, Bingo!" How many in a row for bingo? Five. What do you write in the box? Your friend's name. Now, phonics. Don't you. Don-chu. The t and the y join. Take off. Tay-koff. All over. Aw-low-ver. This summer. Say the s sound only once. Have you ever played bingo in English?

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, Have you ever made sushi? Today, we use two big skills from Stage 3. We explain, and we give advice. Do you remember the Green Laboratory? We said, This chair is made of wood. And in the Village of Springs, we said, You should drink more water. Now, Riko shows Aino an origami frog. It's made of paper. You should try it! Say it with me. It's made of paper. You should try it! Wonderful! Then Haru shows Mateo a kendama. This is a kendama. It's used for playing. Mateo tries, but the ball falls. Haru says, It's a little difficult. You should practice every day. Let's read the label on the kendama box. "Kendama. A Japanese toy. It's made of wood. There is a ball on a string and three cups. Swing the ball up and catch it in a cup. It looks easy, but it's difficult at first. Practice for ten minutes every day. Soon you can do amazing tricks!" What is it made of? Wood. How many cups are there? Three. Look! The bridge is shining. The green color is back! Now, phonics. Keep in touch. Kee-pin-touch. I want to SWIM in the SEA. To is weak. Origami. English speakers use this Japanese word too. Video. VID-e-o. Say the VID part strongly. You should try it, too!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, It's made of paper. You should try it! Today, Iris shows us a big map on the bridge. It's a map of our journey. Look! There is the Tower of Messages, the Amber Library, and the Green Laboratory. There is the Cloudtop Railway, the Cave of Riddles, the Theater of Echoes, and the Village of Springs. Haru smiles and says, I've traveled to many places. Say it with me. I've traveled to many places. Wonderful! Riko points at the map and says, We've been to a tower, a library, a laboratory, and a cave! Kiko asks, Which place was your favorite? Birimo says, The Village of Springs. The food was so good! Let's read the words under the map. "Stage 3 Journey Map. You started at the Tower of Messages. You wrote emails and made phone calls. You rode a train above the clouds. lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, I've traveled to many places. Today, Iris asks a big question. What can you do now? Think about the start of Stage 3. At the Tower of Messages, Haru was nervous on the phone. Now he says, I can make phone calls in English now. Say it with me. I can make phone calls in English now. Great! Riko says, Before, I couldn't write emails. Now I can! Kiko says, I can tell stories in English. Birimo says, I can order three desserts in English! Ha ha. Let's read Kiko's list. "Things I Can Do Now. I can make phone calls and leave messages. I can write emails to a pen pal. I can tell a story with First, Then, and Suddenly. I can explain how things are made. I can give helpful advice to my friends. I can't speak perfectly yet, but I'm not afraid anymore!" Can Kiko write emails? Yes, she can. Is she afraid now? No, she isn't. Now, phonics. Beautiful. Beauty, change the y to i, plus ful. Helpful. Help plus ful. Only one l! Wonderful. Wonder plus ful. Peaceful. Peace plus ful. Keep the e. You are all wonderful learners!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, I can make phone calls in English now. The Friendship Festival is coming soon. Each of us will give a short speech about friendship. Riko starts her draft. She thinks about Aino, Amara, and Mateo. They live in different countries. They eat different food. But they are our friends. Riko writes, Friends can be different, but we can learn from each other. Say it with me. Friends can be different, but we can learn from each other. Beautiful! Let's read Riko's speech draft. "My Friends on the Bridge. Hello, everyone. My friend Amara taught me Swahili. Jambo means hello! Aino taught me a winter game. Mateo taught me how to draw a funny cat. We are all different, and that is wonderful. Friends can be different, but we can learn from each other. Kindness is the best language. Thank you." What does Jambo mean? Hello. Who taught Riko a winter game? Aino did. Now, phonics. Kindness. Kind plus ness. Happiness. Happy, change the y to i, plus ness. Friendliness. Friendly, y to i, plus ness. Openness. Open plus ness. Two n's! Let's write our speeches with kindness and happiness!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, Friends can be different, but we can learn from each other. Today is rehearsal day on the bridge. There is a small stage in Friendship Plaza. Kiko goes first. She reads her speech very fast, and she only looks at her paper. I give her some tips. Speak clearly. Smile at the audience. Say it with me. Speak clearly. Smile at the audience. Great! Then I say, Look up from your paper. Kiko says, OK, I'll try. Remember the theater and the springs? Take a deep breath. Don't hurry. Take your time. Iris hangs a list of speech tips next to the stage. Let's read it. "Five Speech Tips. One, speak clearly and slowly. Two, look up from your paper. Three, smile at the audience. Four, stand up straight. Five, if you make a mistake, don't worry. Just take a breath and go on. Your friends are here to help you. Enjoy your speech!" What is tip number two? Look up from your paper. What do you do after a mistake? Take a breath and go on. Now, phonics. Excitement. Excite plus ment. Keep the e. Argument. Argue, drop the e, plus ment. Enjoyment. Enjoy plus ment. Amazement. Amaze plus ment. Keep the e again. Kiko, you can do it!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, Speak clearly. Smile at the audience. Today is the big day. It's the Friendship Festival on the Rainbow Bridge! Children from many countries are here. Iris opens the festival. She says, Welcome to the friendship festival! Say it with me. Welcome to the friendship festival! Fantastic! Then Haru says, Let's share our songs, games, and food! Kiko gives her speech. She speaks clearly and smiles. Everyone claps. Mateo brings a piñata. Aino teaches a dance. Amara sings a song in Swahili. Birimo shares onigiri, but first, he eats three! Let's read the festival program. "Friendship Festival Program. At one, opening words from Iris. At half past one, friendship speeches. At two, songs from many countries. At half past two, games, like the piñata and the paper crane contest. At three, food from around the world. Please share, smile, and make new friends!" What time are the speeches? At half past one. What happens at three? Food from around the world. Look up! The bridge is shining blue and indigo now. Now, phonics. Disagreement. Dis plus agree plus ment. Meet you. Meet-chu! Can I ask a question? Can is small and quick. Haiku. A short Japanese poem. What a wonderful festival!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, Welcome to the friendship festival! The festival was a big success. Now, our new friends are going home soon. So we're writing letters. Haru writes to his pen pal Leo, and Riko writes to Aino. Haru starts his letter like this. Dear friend, thank you for sharing your culture with me. Say it with me. Dear friend, thank you for sharing your culture with me. Great! Then he writes, I enjoyed learning about your school. At the end, he writes, Please write back soon. Your friend, Haru. Remember, we don't write our address or our school name. Let's read Riko's letter to Aino. "Dear Aino, Thank you for sharing your culture with me. I enjoyed learning about your school. I was surprised to hear you start school at age seven! Your winter game was so much fun. Someday, I want to see the long summer days in Finland. Could you send me a photo of the snow? Please write back soon. Your friend, Riko" When do children in Finland start school? At age seven. What does Riko ask for? A photo of the snow. Now, phonics. Piano. pi-AN-o. Sushi. A Japanese word in English. Let's ask them to help. Them is small and quick. Could you. Could-joo. Thankfulness. Thank plus ful plus ness. My heart is full of thankfulness!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, Dear friend, thank you for sharing your culture with me. Today, Iris has an idea. She says, This bridge connects many countries. Let's make a question box for children around the world! Good questions help us learn. Kiko asks her first question. What do children in your country do for fun? Say it with me. What do children in your country do for fun? Excellent! Haru asks, What time does school start in your country? Riko asks, What's a popular food in your country? Mateo answers, Tacos are popular in Mexico. Then Riko asks a follow-up question. What do you put in your tacos? Let's read the card on the question box. "The World Question Box. Write one question on a card. Ask about school, food, games, or holidays. Good questions start with What, When, Where, Why, or How. Please don't ask for names or addresses. Every week, children from other countries will answer. Then you can ask a follow-up question!" What words do good questions start with? What, When, Where, Why, or How. What should you not ask for? Names or addresses. Now, phonics. Calendar. CAL-en-dar. Kimono. A Japanese word in English. Do you want rice or bread? Or is small and quick. Take care. Say the k sound only once. Unhelpful. Un plus help plus ful. Keep asking good questions!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, What do children in your country do for fun? Today, we are writing an introduction to Japan for the World Question Box. Riko starts with a big fact. Japan has four seasons. Say it with me. Japan has four seasons. Wonderful! Then she writes about her town. In my town, there is a big festival in summer. A good introduction has a beginning, some facts, and an ending. Let's read Riko's draft. "My Japan. Japan has four seasons. In spring, you can see cherry blossoms. In summer, we watch fireworks. In fall, the leaves turn red and yellow. In winter, it snows in many places. In my town, there is a big festival in summer. People in Japan say itadakimasu before meals. It means thank you for the food. Please visit Japan someday!" What can you see in spring? Cherry blossoms. What does itadakimasu mean? Thank you for the food. Count the sentences. There are nine. Perfect! Now, phonics. Hamburger. HAM-bur-ger. Judo. A Japanese word in English. We eat lunch at school. At is small and quick. Made of. Made-of, the words hold hands. Unhappiness. Un plus happy, change the y to i, plus ness. Japan is a wonderful place to introduce!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, Japan has four seasons. Today is our goodbye walk on the Rainbow Bridge. Kiko gives Amara a little box of mochi. She explains, Mochi is a kind of rice cake. I think you'll love it because it's soft and sweet. Say it with me. Mochi is a kind of rice cake. I think you'll love it because it's soft and sweet. Great! Haru adds, We eat it to celebrate New Year. Amara says, Asante! That means thank you. Then Birimo stops and points far away. Look! What's that light over there? Riko says, It must be a lighthouse! Iris smiles and says, Yes. That is the Lighthouse of Ideas. Let's read Iris's goodbye card. "Dear friends, Thank you for visiting the Rainbow Bridge. You shared your food, your games, and your kind words. Now six colors are bright again. Tomorrow, the last color will come back. Far away, you can see a light. It shines from a lighthouse by the sea. Follow the light, and keep sharing your ideas. Love, Iris" How many colors are bright now? Six. Where does the light come from? A lighthouse by the sea. Now, phonics. Pajamas. pa-JA-mas. Manga. A Japanese word in English. What do you think of my idea? Of is small and quick. All over. All-over, the words hold hands. Disrespectful. Dis plus respect plus ful. What a beautiful goodbye walk!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, Mochi is a kind of rice cake. I think you'll love it because it's soft and sweet. Today is the grand finale on the Rainbow Bridge. All our friends stand together. Aino says Moi, Amara says Jambo, and Mateo says Hola. They are different words, but they all mean hello. Haru says, Our languages are different, but our hearts are the same. Say it with me. Our languages are different, but our hearts are the same. Fantastic! Suddenly, the last color comes back. Violet! Now the bridge shines in all seven colors. Iris gives us a special badge. Let's read it. "Rainbow Bridge Friendship Badge. This badge is for Haru, Riko, Kiko, and Birimo. You explained Japan, shared your opinions, and listened to new friends. You made the bridge shine again. Congratulations! You finished Stage 3. Keep in touch with your friends, and keep your hearts open. From Iris" What color came back last? Violet. What did they finish? Stage 3. We say, Thank you, Iris! Thank you, everyone! Then we look at the light far away. Next stop, the Lighthouse of Ideas! Now, phonics. Volunteer. vol-un-TEER. Karaoke. A Japanese word in English. I like summer and winter. And is small and quick. Keep in touch. Keep-in-touch. Unkindness. Un plus kind plus ness. Friendliness. Friendly, change the y to i, plus ness. See you at the lighthouse!
